chunks: Jamil ibn Darraj asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

About an Imam of a people who has become junub, and he does not have with him enough water for ghusl, while they have water with which they perform wudu, so some of them perform wudu and he leads them.
He said: "No. Rather, the Imam should perform tayammum and lead them. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made the earth a purifier just as He has made water a purifier."

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: entered the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْأَرْضَ طَهُورًا: the earth as a means of ritual purification
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: the full ritual bath required after janabah
key_terms.الْمَاءَ طَهُورًا: water as a means of ritual purification
key_terms.يَؤُمُّهُمْ: he leads them in congregational prayer
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum, dry ablution with earth

ai.seo_question: Can a junub Imam lead congregational prayer with tayammum when there is not enough water for ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning congregational salat when the Imam is in janabah and lacks sufficient water for ghusl. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rules that the Imam should perform tayammum and then lead the prayer, affirming that earth is a valid means of ritual purification just as water is.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1123 - Jamil ibn Darraj asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)

about an Imam who becomes ritually impure (junub) and does not have enough water to perform the full ritual bath (ghusl), while the rest of the congregation has water to perform ablution (wudu). He asked whether some of them should perform wudu and then allow the Imam to lead.

Abu Abdullah (as) replied: "No, but the Imam should perform tayammum (dry ablution) and lead them, for Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has made the earth a purifier just as He has made water a purifier”.
